goals: Mechanistic: quantify how elevation controls snowmelt-onset day-of-year across the Naches at the resolvable (~12 km) forcing scale
Validation: compare simulated SWE and melt-onset timing against the 6 SNOTEL stations

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates snowpack (H2OSNO, QSNOMELT, SNOW) and outputs enough to derive per-site melt-onset DOY and to compare SWE against SNOTEL; NLDAS forcing carries a coarse orographic elevation signal.

answerable: Per-station snowmelt-onset DOY and peak-SWE timing at each SNOTEL location (validation against measured SWE)
The BASIN-SCALE elevation control on melt onset, resolved only across stations/columns that fall in DISTINCT ~12 km NLDAS cells

not_answerable.aspect: Local lapse rate between stations on the same ridge that are <12 km apart
not_answerable.why: Default NLDAS-2 forcing is ~12 km with nearest-cell assignment and no within-cell lapse rate; two nearby same-ridge stations share one cell and receive identical forcing, so their true elevation difference cannot drive a difference in simulated melt onset.
not_answerable.needs: elevation-downscaled / sub-grid forcing with within-cell lapse rate

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Four elevation bands span the 1625 m relief and the rain-snow transition where melt-onset sensitivity is largest; 2 columns per band, each placed in a DISTINCT NLDAS cell, give the minimum needed to trace an across-basin elevation-onset curve while keeping replication above forcing resolution (finer replication would resolve soil, not elevation).
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the 750-1550 m rain-snow transition where melt-onset DOY changes fastest with elevation; ensure exploratory columns occupy separate 12 km NLDAS cells so elevation (not identical forcing) drives the contrast.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 per band, in different NLDAS cells, to check within-band spread of the coarse forcing gradient.

sampling_plan.reason: One column co-located at each SNOTEL station to validate simulated SWE and melt-onset DOY against measured SWE; count fixed by observation availability.
Anchor the low, largely rain-dominated end of the elevation-onset curve.
Isolate the elevation band where melt-onset timing is most sensitive to temperature/precip phase.
Trace mid-upper elevation melt onset across distinct NLDAS cells.
Anchor the persistent-snow end; expect latest onset but note 12 km cells underestimate ridgetop SWE.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — one ELM column per station; expect underestimation at high/ridgetop stations because 12 km cells average over terrain
validation_design.metric: bias and RMSE on peak SWE; correlation on daily SWE

validation_design.target_variable: snowmelt-onset day-of-year (derived from H2OSNO decline / QSNOMELT onset)
validation_design.observation_source: SNOTEL SWE (6 stations) — onset derived from observed SWE recession
validation_design.comparison: co-located per-station DOY over multiple winters; also regress onset DOY vs elevation across the stations that lie in distinct NLDAS cells
validation_design.metric: DOY bias; slope of onset-vs-elevation (days per 100 m) with the caveat that same-cell stations cannot be distinguished
validation_design.n_validation_points: 6 (fewer distinct forcing cells if stations share cells)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, short (1-2 yr) snow/soil burn-in, multi-winter analysis window

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled / sub-grid forcing with within-cell lapse rate
requires_capabilities.why: Nearest-cell 12 km NLDAS gives identical forcing to same-ridge stations <12 km apart
requires_capabilities.blocks: Resolving the LOCAL between-station lapse rate — the primary request

requires_capabilities.why: Onset day is not a native output field; must be derived from SWE recession / melt-flux threshold consistently for model and SNOTEL
requires_capabilities.blocks: Quantitative melt-onset comparison and elevation regression

requires_capabilities.why: Needed to pin validation columns and compare SWE/onset

assumptions: SNOTEL station coordinates and elevations are supplied by the downstream expander; I do not invent them.
Snowmelt onset is a fast seasonal state, so a short (1-2 yr) burn-in suffices; deep water-table spin-up is unnecessary for this question.
Multiple winters within 1980-2018 will be analyzed so onset DOY is a distribution across years, not a single-year artifact.
SSURGO native soil is used per column; soil is not a stratification axis here since the driver of interest is elevation via forcing.
open_questions: How many of the 6 SNOTEL stations actually fall in DISTINCT NLDAS 12 km cells? This sets the true number of independent elevation points for the melt-onset regression.
Is a within-cell forcing lapse-rate downscaling planned? If so, the local same-ridge lapse-rate goal becomes answerable.
Which winters (years) should define the melt-onset climatology — full 1980-2018, or a recent subset?
